mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries allows the model to generate two AuditEntries with the same (auditApp, eventType) pair. The injected violation forces exactly that state, so AppendOnly and the audit completeness assertions find a counterexample: the 'one ae' cardinality in AuditCompleteness becomes false when there are two submitted-event entries for the same application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.auditApp = ae2.auditApp and ae1.eventType = ae2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OnePendingPerCustomer allows two distinct LoanApplications for the same customer both to have status PendingReview. The injected violation forces this instance to exist, directly violating FR_005_OnePendingPerCustomer.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePendingViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.appCustomer = a2.appCustomer and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_DeciderIsStaff permits a Decision whose decidedBy user has CustomerRole. The injected violation forces a Decision made by a customer-role user, directly falsifying FR_009_DecisionReasonAndStaffOnly (which requires all deciders to be BankStaffRole) and exposing the LeastPrivilege violation that customers should not be able to post decisions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CustomerDecides { some d: Decision | d.decidedBy.role = CustomerRole }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AtMostOneDecisionPerApplication allows two Decision atoms to point at the same LoanApplication, modelling a double-decision race. The injected violation forces this state, which is exactly what ConcurrencySafety and FR_011_DecisionImmutability are meant to exclude.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DoubleDecision { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.forApplication = d2.forApplication }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuditActorAttribution allows audit entries to record an actor whose role does not match the event type — e.g., a bank staff member as actor on a SubmittedEvt, or a customer as actor on an ApprovedEvt. The injected violation creates a SubmittedEvt entry whose actor is a BankStaffRole user, falsifying AttributionCorrectness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MisattributedActor { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.eventType = SubmittedEvt and ae.actor.role = BankStaffRole }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_PermissionMatrix leaves the Allowed relation unconstrained. The injected violation adds the forbidden cell CustomerRole->PostDecision, directly falsifying LeastPrivilege and FR_015_RoleBasedAccess, and also breaks PermissionCompleteness (cardinality check fails) and PermissionGrounding (extra ungrounded cell present).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CustomerCanDecide { CustomerRole -> PostDecision in PermMatrix.Allowed }
